info.title: Larpinq
info.description:
The JSON API of Larpinq, the live action role-play app for Nextcloud: character sheets and builds, events with registrations, check-in and XP awards, worlds, settings and the setup wizard. The characters, events and other objects themselves are stored in OpenRegister and read and written through its API; this document covers the endpoints Larpinq adds on top.

Every path is served under `/api/v1/`, the version this document describes. The unversioned `/api/` paths keep working, are deprecated, and name their `/api/v1/` successor in a `Link` header next to a `Deprecation` header. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`), and every response carries an `API-Version` header. Paths that implement an external standard keep the formats of that standard and are not described here.

get.summary: Whether the caller may apply builds to character sheets: game masters and admins
get.description: Whether the caller may apply builds to character sheets: game masters and admins. The build page shows its Apply action on this answer; the write itself is checked by OpenRegister and the requirement listener.

get.summary: The check of one build: the requirement report and the stat sheet of the character as it would be with the build's skill
get.description: The check of one build: the requirement report and the stat sheet of the character as it would be with the build's skills, items and conditions. The character's own XP awards count, so the budget is real. Nothing is written.

200.description: `{build, character, report, stats, lists, changes}`, or 404.

get.summary: Whether the signed-in user is a game master for the character page's game master actions
get.description: Whether the signed-in user may record a requirement override or reject a character: game masters and admins. The character page shows its Override a requirement and Reject actions on this answer; the writes themselves are checked by the requirement listener and the lifecycle.

get.summary: Recompute the skill-requirement report for one character on demand
get.description: Recompute the skill-requirement report for one character on demand.  Returns the structured validation result (unmet prerequisites, overridden entries, dependent-now-unmet skills from past removals/global edits, the XP budget block). Read-only: it never writes. Authorization is delegated to OpenRegister via the fetch, a user who cannot read the character via the OR-backed fetch gets a 404, so this endpoint exposes nothing the caller could not already read through the OR objects API.

200.description: The requirement report, or an error response.

post.summary: Buy an item for a character with its in-game money
post.description: Buy an item for a character with its in-game money. Adds the item and takes its price in gold, silver and copper in one write; each coin is paid from its own purse. The character's owner or a game master only. A purchase the character cannot pay is refused with 409 and changes nothing.

post.summary: Submit a rejected character again
post.description: Submit a rejected character again: it goes back to waiting for approval and the game masters are told. The character's owner or a game master only; a character that is not rejected is refused with 409 and changes nothing.

get.summary: The stat sheet of one character
get.description: The stat sheet of one character.

get.summary: Whether the signed-in user may download event run sheets; the event page shows its "Download run sheet" action on this answer
get.description: Whether the signed-in user may download event run sheets: game masters and admins, the same rule as the download. The event page shows its "Download run sheet" action on this answer.

post.summary: Record or update a participant's attendance for an event (GM-only)
post.description: Record or update a participant's attendance for an event (GM-only).  Server-authoritative: the acting user MUST be in the `gamemasters` group or a Nextcloud admin, the `(event, character)` pair MUST be a confirmed participant, and `checkedInAt` / `checkedInBy` are stamped from the server clock and session, never read from the request body (anti-forgery, the rule shared with `xpAward.awardedAt` / `awardedBy`). Persistence and the schema-level RBAC are OR-delegated (ADR-022); this controller adds no parallel attendance-write auth path. Degrades to a 424 when the `larping_attendance` schema is absent rather than throwing.

200.description: The persisted attendance record, or an error.

get.summary: The proposed casting of the event (game masters only)
get.description: The best overall casting of the characters open for casting on the event to the players who ranked them: as many ranked matches as possible, then the lowest total rank, then the most first choices, then earlier sign-ups. Lists the players left without a ranked character and, per open character, how often it was ranked at each rank. Writes nothing.

200.description: The pairs, the unmatched players and the rank counts.

post.summary: Confirm the casting (game masters only)
post.description: Writes the pairs the game master kept or changed: each character gets the registration's player as owner and leaves casting, and the registration gets the character. A pair outside the event, a pair that repeats a registration or character, or a failed write is refused by name; the other pairs are written.

200.description: The pairs written and the pairs refused with the reason.

post.summary: Check a participant in by the code of their registration (GM-only)
post.description: Check a participant in by the code of their registration (GM-only). The game master check runs first; then only `code` is read from the body. 200 `{status: checked-in, name, character}` on a first use, 200 `{status: already, at, by}` on a second, 409 `{status: not-accepted}` for a registration that is not accepted, 404 `{status: unknown}` for an unknown code or one of another event. Rate limited per user.

200.description: The participant checked in, or when and by whom they already were.

code.description: The check-in code as typed or scanned.

get.summary: How many accepted registrations of the event chose each ticket type and option
get.description: How many accepted registrations of the event chose each ticket type and option.

200.description: `{ticketTypes: [{id, name, role, count}], options: [{id, name, category, count}]}`, or 401, 403.

get.summary: Read the check-in roster for an event
get.description: Read the check-in roster for an event.  Read access is open to any authenticated app user, the roster is read-only for players; the `isGm` flag tells the client whether to render the check-in controls. Degrades gracefully: when the `larping_attendance` schema (or OpenRegister) is unavailable the participant list is still returned with `attendanceAvailable=false` and no per-row status, so the event page never breaks (DocuDesk / Forms-leaf degradation pattern).

200.description: The roster payload, or an error response.

get.description: The award roster of an event: participants, attendance, existing awards and the default ticks. Game masters only.

get.description: The event's feedback form and window, how many invited participants answered, who has not, and the link to the results in Nextcloud Forms. `answered` and `notAnswered` are null when Forms cannot tell. Game masters only.

get.summary: The character-sheet templates for the Download as PDF dialog
get.description: The character-sheet templates for the Download as PDF dialog.  Administrator only, like downloadPdf(): the header action reads this endpoint as its visibility predicate, so the action is hidden for everyone who could not download anyway, and when the document app is absent (`available: false`).  Deliberately NOT `@NoAdminRequired`, for the same reason as downloadPdf(): only an administrator may download a sheet today. `#[NoCSRFRequired]` because it is a read-only GET that the header action's visibility probe fetches, like downloadPdf's GET.

get.description: The events the player was checked in at, newest first, and how many. Game masters see every player's; a player sees only their own.

get.summary: Get current Larpinq settings
get.description: Get current Larpinq settings.

post.summary: Legacy alias for `update()`, `POST /api/settings`
post.description: Legacy alias for `update()`, `POST /api/settings`.  The canonical AppHost route table still ships `settings#create` for the pre-ADR-066 `index/create/load` dialect, and Larpinq's own frontend still POSTs to it (`src/store/modules/settings.js::saveSettings()` and `src/views/settings/Settings.vue`), so this route must stay reachable and must keep writing (ADR-029).  The delegation is one-way and behaviour-preserving: the response payload is byte-identical to what this method returned before `update()` existed.  CSRF protection is required, this is a state-mutating admin POST.  Auth posture: unchanged. This method keeps its own (absent = Nextcloud default admin + CSRF) posture rather than inheriting anything from `update()`, because SecurityMiddleware only evaluates attributes on the DISPATCHED method, delegation in the body is invisible to it.  The `NoCSRFRequired` annotation was dropped here for #206. It is spelled mid-sentence on purpose: Nextcloud's ControllerMethodReflector matches `/^\h+\*\h+@(?P<annotation>[A-Z]\w+)((?P<parameter>.*))?$/m`, so a line that BEGINS with the tag registers it as present no matter what the rest of the sentence says, which is how #206 stayed open here for months.

put.summary: Update Larpinq settings, the canonical write
put.description: Update Larpinq settings, the canonical write.  This is the `settings#update` half of OpenRegister's canonical AppHost settings dialect (`\OCA\OpenRegister\AppHost\Controller\GenericSettingsControllerBase::update()`), reached over `PUT /api/settings`. Larpinq ships its own SettingsController, so `AppHost\Bootstrap::aliasControllerUnlessLeafDefinesIt()` never aliases the generic in and this leaf owes the method itself.  The body is the one that used to live in `create()`: it hands the full request parameter bag to `\OCA\Larpinq\Service\SettingsService::updateSettings()`, which whitelists it against `SettingsService::CONFIG_KEYS` and writes the accepted string/int values to `IAppConfig` under the `larpinq` app id, then returns the re-read settings map. Nothing outside that whitelist is persisted, so PUT writes exactly what POST wrote.  CSRF protection is required, this is a state-mutating admin write.  Auth posture: no auth attribute, deliberately identical to `create()`. Nextcloud's default for an attribute-free controller method is "admin session required, CSRF token required", which is the posture this instance-wide configuration write needs. `@NoCSRFRequired` was removed from the write path to close the CSRF-forgery surface (closes #206) and is not reintroduced here. Net privilege change of this commit: zero.

post.summary: Canonical AppHost alias for `reimport()`
post.description: Canonical AppHost alias for `reimport()`.  `OpenRegister\AppHost\Routes::standard()` declares `settings#load`, and the local fallback in appinfo/routes.php reproduces it, so the route existed here with no method behind it: every POST to /api/settings/load was a dispatch-time 500. Pinned by CanonicalSettingsRouteContractTest, which is what caught it.  larpinq spells the same operation `reimport()`, so this delegates rather than duplicating it, the way `create()` delegates to `update()`. The four sibling apps that already carry `load()` do the same force re-import.

post.summary: Re-import the Larpinq configuration from the JSON file
post.description: Re-import the Larpinq configuration from the JSON file.  CSRF protection is required, this is a state-mutating admin POST.  The `NoCSRFRequired` annotation was dropped here for #206, and is spelled mid-sentence for the reason given on `create()`: a docblock line that begins with the tag re-registers it.

post.summary: Run a privileged server-side setup action
post.description: Run a privileged server-side setup action.

post.summary: Persist app-config values from a `choice` / `config-fields` step
post.description: Persist app-config values from a `choice` / `config-fields` step.  Larpinq's wizard has no config-only steps today, but the endpoint is provided for parity with the abstract wizard contract so future steps can write config without a new controller.

get.summary: Report per-step setup status for the wizard
get.description: Report per-step setup status for the wizard.  The wizard has no required step any more: provisioning moved to the admin settings page (wizard-dataset-card-load), where the `provision` action still runs. `provisioned` travels as information, not as a step, so the admin page and a support check can read it.

get.summary: Search the remote store
get.description: Search the remote store. Login-required through an in-body guard so an anonymous caller gets an explicit 401 rather than a login redirect. Returns normalised cards and a generic outcome, NEVER the registry URL or token. With no registry configured the engine answers `not_configured` WITHOUT making a network call, which is what lets the page fall back to the app's built-in items (ADR-080 Decision 4). Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.

post.summary: Install one store item into this instance
post.description: Install one store item into this instance. Administrative: the components written are the shape of the work every handler then operates against. The write runs as the calling administrator and NOT through `runAsSystem()`. That elevation is for operations whose inputs originate from code or the app's own seed data; a store payload is neither, it comes off the network. Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.

post.summary: Publish one item of the app's store schema to its configured registry
post.description: Publish one item of the app's store schema to its configured registry. The body is `{item: {...}}`, an object that carries its `slug`. Only a user the app's publish groups admit may publish (StoreActionAuthorizer::canPublish); the engine then sends the slug and the declared publish fields, and nothing else (GenericStoreService). Needs a signed-in Nextcloud user.

get.description: Whether the signed-in user may copy worlds; the world page shows its "Copy world" action on this answer.

post.description: Create an invite link for one role, valid `days` days (default 7) for `maxUses` people (default 1). The plain token and the link are in this answer only. Game masters only.

post.summary: The role and state of the invite a token opens
post.description: The role and state (valid, expired, used-up, revoked) of the invite a token opens, for the landing page. Signed-in users; rate limited.

post.summary: Join the role of the invite a token opens
post.description: Join the role of a valid invite and the app's user group; the use is recorded. An expired, used-up or revoked invite answers 410 and adds nobody. Signed-in users; rate limited.

post.summary: Revoke an invite
post.description: Revoke an invite: from now on it adds nobody. Game masters only.

get.summary: The members of each role and every invite
get.description: The members of the game master group and each staff role, and every invite with its state. Game masters only.

delete.summary: Remove a member from a role
delete.description: Remove a member from a role. A game master cannot remove themself from the game masters. Game masters only.

get.description: How many people a message to the event's participants reaches, the first ten names and who has no address. Game masters only.

post.summary: Save a message to the event's participants as a draft
post.description: Save a message to the event's participants as a draft. Game masters only.

201.description: The draft message, or 400 without subject or body, 401, 403, 404.

post.summary: Send a draft message to the event's participants
post.description: Queue a draft message: each recipient gets their own mail, 50 per background run. A message is sent once. Game masters only.

202.description: The queued message, or 401, 403, 404, 409 when it was sent before.

post.summary: Create a character for the asserted portal player (portaliq forward)
post.description: The receiver of the portal `createCharacter` endpoint action. Called server to server by portaliq with a signed `X-Portal-Subject` assertion; the assertion is the only credential. The linked player's uuid comes from the assertion's `ownerRef` claim, never from the body, and is written into both `ownerRef` and the required `ocName`. The body carries `name` (required) and `background`.

201.description: The created character's id and name.

503.description: The character could not be saved.

basic_auth.description: A Nextcloud user name with an app password.

API-Version.description: The version of the API that answered, which is the installed app version.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details. Members the endpoint returned before, such as `error` or `message`, are kept.

type.description: A URI that identifies the problem type.

title.description: The HTTP reason phrase of the status.

detail.description: What went wrong, for this occurrence.
